_note: Summoner spells are assigned deterministically in Python (web/advisor/summoners.py), not chosen by the model. They follow a small set of flat rules that do not benefit from reasoning, and leaving them to the model meant re-validating a jungler's Smite on every generation.
_precedence: 1. Jungle role -> Smite is mandatory. Partner is Ghost for the run-down list below, otherwise Flash.
3. Support role -> Ignite + Flash for engage/kill supports (Tank or Assassin class), Heal + Flash for everyone else.
4. Marksman outside the jungle -> Flash + Barrier when the kit has a repositioning ability, Ghost + Flash when it does not.

runDownChampions._why: Champions whose whole pattern is closing distance and staying on a target. Ghost is not a preference for these, it is part of how they work.

marksmenWithMobility._why: Curated deliberately. Both automatic detectors fail here: the champion record's `dash` mechanic tag fires on the word 'charge' (Varus' Piercing Arrow charge-up), and a stricter ability-text scan still mis-reads Jinx, whose Flame Chompers text says it interrupts enemy 'dashes'. Corki fails the opposite way -- Valkyrie reads 'Flies a short distance' and matches no movement keyword at all. Twenty-odd champions is small enough to state outright and easy to correct.

_explicitlyWithout.Jinx: Flame Chompers interrupts enemy dashes; Jinx has no movement ability of her own.
_explicitlyWithout.Varus: Piercing Arrow charges up, it does not move him. No dash in the kit.
_explicitlyWithout.Caitlyn: 90 Caliber Net displaces her, but it is an escape on a long cooldown rather than the in-combat repositioning Barrier assumes.
_explicitlyWithout.Sivir: Movement speed steroid on the ultimate, not a dash.
_explicitlyWithout.Senna: No dash; plays Support and takes the support rule anyway.

engageSupportClasses._why: The user's rule names 'tank supports' for Ignite. Assassin supports (Pyke) belong in the same bucket: they are kill-lane supports, and Heal fits them no better than it fits Leona.

default._why: Not specified by the rules above. Flash plus Ignite is the standard laner pairing and keeps kill pressure, which is what a Mid or Baron laner outside the named lists usually wants. Change here if you want a different fallback.
